title: SHADOWS ON THE SERVER WALL
about: A Ranger breaks into a simulated Dallas data mine and walks one worker, Susan, up Plato's cave: the questions she cannot answer, the guard drone he kicks out of the air, the door nobody wants opened, the screen she turns off, and the noble lie left waiting for his answer.

beats.text: A simulated Dallas, where the clock always reads 6:41. In a vast warehouse, workers sit in rows at screens. The Ranger Walker has broken in, with a hacker's voice in his head.
see: rows of office workers typing at desks
a clock on a factory wall

beats.text: This ain’t oil.
Nah, partner. It’s worse. It’s engagement metrics.
Sir… are you… management?
No ma’am. I’m… maintenance.
Susan. What do you think this place is?
It’s Dallas. We’re doing honest work. We’re… building the future.
What are you mining?
Data.
What is data?
It’s… information.
And what is information for?
It’s for… the company?
And who’s the company?
Careful, cowboy. You’re asking questions in a world built on answers.

beats.ask: I never really asked who it was all for

beats.text: You’re in a cave. A room where they show you shadows and call it life. These screens are the wall. The work is the chain.
A drone descends from the ceiling: the system's courtesy check. Asked what this place is, it pauses a moment too long, then answers. Dallas. Honest work.
see: a camera hanging from a ceiling

beats.text: No. It’s a server. And they’re batteries.
The drone calls this unlicensed advocacy and arms its gun. Justice, it says, is the advantage of the stronger. Walker kicks it out of the air, into a shower of sparks.
see: sparks flying from a broken machine

beats.text: We’re… not supposed to do that.
No. You’re not supposed to see that you can.
Walker grips the locked warehouse door and asks what lies outside. A worker answers without thinking: freedom.
see: a hand on a door handle

beats.text: And if it isn’t freedom?
…Then it’s… the real world?
And if the real world is worse than this?
Then… why leave?
That’s the trick, Walker. They don’t cage you with bars. They cage you with comparisons.

beats.ask: at least here we know where we stand

beats.text: Because it’s yours. Even if it’s ugly. Even if it’s cold. This is a shadow on a server wall. And you’re worth more than somebody else’s electricity.
Then Susan reaches out and turns her terminal off. A crack opens in the air above the workers. Through it: red desert, and real stars.
see: a woman switching off a machine
stars over a desert at night

beats.ask: it was like waking up from a long sleep

beats.text: On the wall, a prompt appears for Walker alone. Execute the noble lie, yes or no. Warning: may cause awakening.
If I hit “Y”… who gets hurt?
Everybody who was comfortable.
